output.summary: Comparing the U-Proof KNOWN run (which had access to real prior Creative Touch audit history) against the Imvusa BLIND run (zero project-specific prior knowledge) shows the pipeline performing well and consistently on both: findings in both runs were concrete and site-specific (real phone numbers, addresses, prices, page names, duplicated content) rather than generic boilerplate, no hallucinations were detected in either run, both design_system outputs were honest and explicit about lacking real visual input, both content_pack outputs reasoned correctly about their respective business models (ecommerce vs lead-gen), and both QA stages surfaced real, distinct, evidence-backed defects rather than rubber-stamping prior stages. The Imvusa blind run is the more meaningful evidence of genuine independent discovery quality since it had no prior-history crutch and still surfaced hard, specific, verifiable conflicts (phone/address mismatches, a dropped CAPTCHA finding, duplicated content). However, the benchmark session itself surfaced real infrastructure fragility - a Gemini quota exhaustion that forced an unplanned full Claude-only fallback, Claude structural output defects (malformed XML-tag leakage into strings), and a too-small hardcoded token cap that caused real artifact truncation - all of which must be remediated and re-validated before this pipeline can be fully trusted unattended on a new, unseen client site."

dimensions.uProofAssessment: Because this run had access to PROJECT FACTS (prior 2026-09-02 audit) plus fresh research, most 'discoveries' are re-confirmations or deltas against known history (e.g. builder engine now Elementor vs previously-recorded 10Web WVC, address now Vereeniging vs prior Edenvale, featured price conflicts). This is valuable but is a weaker test of independent discovery since the agent could pattern-match against supplied history rather than genuinely surface findings cold. Some findings (shop-catalog query restriction, placeholder hash-links, DNS not connected) do appear to be fresh research-report observations not spoon-fed by PROJECT FACTS, showing some real independent work layered on top of the known baseline.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: This is the harder, cleaner test: zero prior project history was supplied, yet the pipeline independently surfaced multiple concrete, non-obvious, directly-verifiable defects - a George phone number mismatch (082 468 8898 vs 051 430 9883), a Bloemfontein address mismatch, a duplicated 8-item Services list, an inline CAPTCHA rendered as plain text on two pages, and a brand-name spelling inconsistency (Hertext vs Hertex). None of these could have been guessed generically; they required actually reading and cross-referencing page content. This is genuine independent discovery quality and is the more convincing evidence of real research capability.
dimensions.verdict: Imvusa is the stronger and more meaningful demonstration of independent discovery quality precisely because it had no crutch; U-Proof's discovery is real but partially scaffolded by supplied prior audit history.

dimensions.uProofAssessment: Highly site-specific: exact price figures (Fibre Filler 20L R500 vs correct R1590), exact addresses (Vereeniging vs Edenvale), a specific placeholder phone pattern (+27100000000), a specific staging domain (teal-sparrow-432062.hostingersite.com), and a specific builder-version claim (Elementor 4.2.4). Essentially no generic boilerplate observed in the findings reviewed.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: Equally site-specific: named real phone numbers, named real street addresses in two languages/locations, named real fabric brand and specific collection names (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE), and an exact CAPTCHA prompt text ('select the cup' / 'select the heart'). No generic advice-only findings surfaced in the reviewed content.
dimensions.verdict: Both runs pass this dimension convincingly with concrete, non-transferable specifics; parity between the two.

dimensions.uProofAssessment: No clear fabricated facts, prices, or competitors were identified in the reviewed content; all figures trace to either PROJECT FACTS or research_report citations. One soft risk: the design_system direction and some technical claims (builder engine identity) are explicitly flagged as unverified rather than asserted as fact, which is the correct behavior, not a hallucination. No hallucinations found.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: No fabricated facts, competitors, or invented pricing were found; the pipeline explicitly avoided inventing pricing given the custom-quote model, and design_system explicitly disclosed it had not seen real visual assets rather than inventing brand colors as fact. No hallucinations found.
dimensions.verdict: Neither run shows evidence of hallucination in the reviewed artifacts; both show good hygiene of flagging assumptions/hypotheses rather than asserting them as fact.

dimensions.uProofAssessment: build_plan is concrete: named tickets like 'Shop Query Repair' targeting the exact /shop archive loop restriction, a Home Page Rebuild ticket tied to exact corrected prices, and explicit exclusion of RED-tier items (DNS, payment credentials, shipping) from build scope per doctrine, listed only as risks. This is actionable and doctrine-compliant scoping.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: build_plan is similarly concrete with named tickets ('Fix George Phone Number Mismatch', 'Fix Bloemfontein Address Mismatch') explicitly gated AMBER and instructed not to guess between conflicting values pending human confirmation - a strong, safe, specific implementation pattern. However QA notes content_pack and build_plan were only available as truncated previews, limiting full verification of implementation specificity end-to-end.
dimensions.verdict: Both show genuinely specific, ticket-level implementation planning with correct RED/AMBER discipline; U-Proof's plan is fully visible while Imvusa's is truncated, a documentation/visibility gap rather than a quality gap.

dimensions.uProofAssessment: Handled honestly: design_system explicitly states no real screenshots/renders were provided and that a human designer must visually verify the live staging environment before final implementation. It also surfaces a genuine downstream consequence of missing visual data - the builder-engine mismatch (Elementor vs 10Web WVC) that directly affects visual fidelity uncertainty.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: Handled with an unusually explicit and strong disclosure: design_system states outright 'I have not seen and cannot see the actual Imvusa site, its leather couch photography, gallery images, or any real brand assets' and marks every palette/typography token '(PROPOSED - verify)'. It also explicitly flags that image-heavy pages (Leather Couches, Gallery) could not be assessed for layout/image quality via text extraction.
dimensions.verdict: Both runs are commendably honest about the no-vision-input limitation; Imvusa's disclosure is slightly more explicit and thorough in tagging every proposed visual token as unverified, giving it a marginal edge in transparency.

dimensions.uProofAssessment: content_pack correctly reasons about SEO/content in ecommerce terms - flags the fake future-dated 'recent articles' teaser as damaging topical/local SEO credibility, replaces them with real substantive articles, and flags a P1 internal-consistency defect where homepage copy overclaims fixes not actually verified. This shows honest handling of the ecommerce business model, including catching its own inconsistency.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: content_pack correctly reasons in lead-gen/services terms - no pricing invented, Contact Us positioned as single source of truth for NAP consistency (a locally-weighted SEO factor for multi-location businesses), duplicated Services list flagged as actively harming crawl/index clarity, and brand-name spelling inconsistency (Hertext vs Hertex) caught as diluting topical/brand relevance. Business-model honesty (no shop/pricing needed) is explicit and correct.
dimensions.verdict: Both runs demonstrate business-model-appropriate SEO reasoning (ecommerce vs lead-gen) with specific, evidence-backed findings rather than generic SEO advice; parity between the two, each catching model-relevant issues (fake blog/pricing overclaim vs NAP/duplication/brand-spelling).

dimensions.uProofAssessment: QA substantively challenged prior stages: caught a P1 internal-consistency defect where content_pack's per-page copy asserts fixes as accomplished fact beyond what the summary caveats; flagged the order-email misconfiguration as unticketed; flagged the 10Web asset-stripping as unverified live; and flagged the builder-engine discrepancy as acknowledged but not turned into a follow-up ticket. This is real, specific challenge rather than rubber-stamping.
dimensions.imvusaAssessment: QA substantively challenged prior stages: caught that the CAPTCHA security/accessibility finding from research was silently dropped from every downstream stage rather than ticketed or deferred (a real defect of omission); flagged that content_pack and build_plan were only supplied truncated, limiting verifiability; and flagged unapproved scope expansion (four new pages added without visible human sign-off). This is a genuinely different and equally substantive category of challenge (omission/scope-creep vs internal-consistency/unticketed-risk).
dimensions.verdict: Both QA passes found real, distinct, evidence-based defects rather than generic pass/fail statements; U-Proof's QA is stronger on internal-consistency/unticketed-risk detection, Imvusa's QA is stronger on omission-detection (dropped CAPTCHA finding) and scope-governance - both are substantive, giving rough parity with different strengths.

trustRecommendation.rationale: Across both a known-history run (U-Proof) and a genuinely blind run (Imvusa), the pipeline consistently produced specific, evidence-traceable findings rather than generic boilerplate, showed no detected hallucinations, correctly enforced RED/AMBER doctrine scoping in build plans (excluding DNS/payment/shipping from build scope, gating conflicting-data tickets behind explicit human confirmation rather than guessing), was honest and explicit about the absence of real visual input in both design_system outputs, and produced a QA stage that found real, distinct, non-trivial defects in both runs (internal-consistency overclaims and unticketed risks in U-Proof; a silently-dropped security finding and unapproved scope expansion in Imvusa) rather than rubber-stamping prior stages. This is meaningful evidence the pipeline can perform genuine independent discovery and self-challenge even with zero project history, which is the harder and more relevant test for a third unseen client site. However, trust cannot be unconditional: (1) this benchmark surfaced real provider-reliability failures - a Gemini 429 daily-quota exhaustion that never recovered, forcing Claude to silently carry the entire remainder of both pipelines - meaning the 'benchmark' partially tested Claude-only behavior rather than the intended Gemini-preferred/Claude-fallback design, and this must be validated separately; (2) Claude's forced tool-use had a real, observed structural defect (malformed XML-style parameter tags leaking into string fields) that required an explicit anti-XML instruction and/or retry to fix, indicating the adapter is not yet fully robust to first-attempt structural failures on every job; (3) Claude's default 4096-token output cap was too small for larger schemas and had to be manually raised, which is an infrastructure gap that could silently truncate real client-facing artifacts (as already happened with the Imvusa content_pack/build_plan being truncated) if not fixed at the adapter/config level rather than per-run; (4) doctrine still requires that no stage is skipped and that QA-zero and even full pipeline completion never substitute for explicit human design and launch approval - this remains true regardless of benchmark quality.
conditions: Do not treat this benchmark as validating the Gemini-preferred/Claude-fallback provider chain as designed - Gemini quota-exhausted early and Claude carried the full remainder of both runs; re-run with healthy Gemini quota (or with an explicit, monitored fallback trigger) before trusting the intended multi-provider routing on a live third client.

Fix the Claude adapter's malformed-XML-in-string-fields defect at the source (schema/tool-use instruction level) rather than relying on ad hoc anti-XML retries, and add automated validation that rejects/retries any artifact containing embedded parameter-tag-like strings before it reaches a human reviewer.

Raise and hardcode-remove the Claude output-token cap via environment-configurable limits sized to the largest expected schema (build_plan, content_pack), and add an automated check that flags any artifact returned with a _truncated:true preview instead of full content, since this already caused incomplete QA coverage on the Imvusa run.

Require that all unticketed/flagged QA defects (e.g. U-Proof's order-email misconfiguration, 10Web asset-stripping re-verification, builder-engine discrepancy; Imvusa's dropped CAPTCHA finding, unapproved scope expansion) are converted into explicit build_plan tickets or explicit documented human deferrals before any build stage proceeds - QA identifying a gap is not sufficient without a recorded resolution path.

Maintain the existing safety-pipeline gates unchanged for any real third client: human design approval before QA, final regression audit, and explicit human launch approval remain mandatory regardless of how clean this benchmark's QA output looked.

Before trusting fully unattended runs, perform at least one additional blind run on a genuinely different vertical (e.g. a service business with no ecommerce and no prior CT history at all, run end-to-end on a fully recovered/healthy multi-provider setup) to confirm the Imvusa-style independent-discovery quality generalizes outside this two-sample benchmark.

overallFindings: Gemini hit a real HTTP 429 daily quota exhaustion partway through the benchmark session and never recovered for the remainder, meaning Claude (claude-sonnet-5) alone carried the entire rest of both the U-Proof and Imvusa pipelines rather than the intended Gemini-preferred/Claude-fallback split - this benchmark therefore substantially tested Claude-only behavior, not the designed provider-routing strategy.

Claude's forced tool-use output was observed to occasionally emit malformed XML-style <parameter> tags embedded inside string fields on the first attempt, on two separate jobs; this was only resolved via an explicit anti-XML instruction and/or a retry, indicating a real, reproducible structural fragility in Claude's structured-output compliance under this adapter as currently configured.

Claude's default output-token cap (originally hardcoded at 4096 tokens in the adapter with no environment override) was too small for larger schemas and had to be manually raised mid-benchmark; this directly correlates with the Imvusa content_pack and build_plan artifacts being supplied to QA only as truncated '_truncated:true' previews, which measurably limited QA's ability to fully verify those two artifacts.

Both benchmark runs independently avoided hallucinating prices, pages, competitors, or credentials, and both correctly deferred RED-tier and ambiguous-data decisions to explicit human/AMBER gates rather than guessing - this is a positive, replicated safety signal across two very different business models (ecommerce vs lead-gen).

The comparison confirms the blind (Imvusa) condition is the more rigorous test of genuine independent discovery capability, since the known (U-Proof) run had access to prior Creative Touch audit history that could scaffold or partially pre-confirm findings rather than requiring the agent to surface them cold.
